failure_analysis.what: SessionConfig caching produced benchmark geomean 9.381 μs/op vs current best 9.233 μs/op — a 1.6% regression (within typical JMH noise).
failure_analysis.why: The Caffeine cache already intercepts findVertexById/findVerticesByLabel/neighbors for both AGE and Neo4j at ~0.015 μs. Those dominate the geomean, leaving write/traversal paths (shortestPath/allPaths/createEdge/createVertex) as the only places where SessionConfig allocation savings could matter. SessionConfig.builder().withDatabase().build() is a cheap immutable object allocation; it is negligible relative to the hundreds-of-μs per-call cost of a real Bolt round-trip. The measured variance in the uncached benchmarks (e.g. neo4j_createEdge error ±2797, age_createEdge error ±3890) is far larger than any savings from avoiding a handful of builder allocations.
failure_analysis.lesson: Micro-allocation caching inside a driver-session path is dwarfed by network I/O variance; when geomean is already pinned by cached 0.015 μs operations, only changes that shave meaningful work off the slowest (write) sub-scores can move the primary score. Future planners: focus optimizations on the write path sub-scores (createEdge/createVertex) where Caffeine cannot help, or extend caching to additional read-like operations.
